thread:
alex: heads-up — saw a weird fallback decision on /v1/generate for tenant acme. headers included X-Fallback-Priority: prefer-primary but the request ended up on the smallest backup model.
ria: can you paste the exact headers + route that matched?
zach: also include gateway log lines if possible, that helps. usually fallback honor order: route overrides > tenant policy > global, but we recently changed capacity scoring.
alex: incoming headers:
```
X-Tenant: acme
X-Fallback-Priority: prefer-primary
x-rl-region: us-east-1
User-Agent: client/2.1
```
Route matched: /v1/generate -> policy=low-latency pool=p100-prod
Gateway log snippets: 
```
[14:12:02.123] matched route /v1/generate policy=low-latency tenant=acme
[14:12:02.130] circuit_breaker(p100-prod) count=120 err_rate=0.32 tripped
[14:12:02.131] fallback_chain_start tenant=acme hint_header=X-Fallback-Priority=prefer-primary
[14:12:02.132] fallback_choice -> redwood-small (cost_based)
```
maya: looks like the CB tripped first — then the chooser fell back to cost_based pick. we have a rule that header hints are only advisory unless "allow_header_override" is true on the tenant or route.
ria: that's the crux — some tenants (acme) expect header-level quality preference to win. current behavior is surprising. can we let a route opt into honoring header hints with safe guards?
zach: we can, but we need constraints: header-override mustn't bypass tenant quota or reserved capacity. policy idea: header_override is allowed when (a) tenant flag=allow-header, (b) model has available capacity and doesn't violate per-model qps, and (c) override_source is recorded in telemetry.
alex: agreed on telemetry. right now traces only show fallback.model and fallback.reason. we should add fields: fallback.header_hint=true/false and fallback.policy_source=(route|tenant|global). also log which check failed if we ignored header.
infra-bot: alert: circuit-breaker p100-prod tripped 2026-03-01T14:12:03Z
maya: UX: console rollout page needs to show the effective fallback chain for a route and which elements are overridable by headers. ops should be able to simulate requests with header hints from console (simulate button)
ria: config suggestion (draft):
```
fallback:
  order: [preferred_model, regional_model, cost_model]
  allow_header_override: true
  header_whitelist: ['acme', 'beta-tenant']
  override_constraints:
    deny_if_quota_violation: true
    require_capacity_check: true
```
zach: +1 but implement as triage steps: header hint -> check quota & capacity -> accept/deny. If denied, log reason and continue chain. Do NOT silently ignore header.
alex: also need to plumb quota decisions into the chooser. right now chooser only sees capacity_score and cost_score; add quota_score that is infinite penalty if override would breach quota.
maya: another idea: graceful-degrade step before swapping to smaller model. chain could be: 1) degrade SLO (allow slightly higher latency), 2) quantize main model (switch to int8 if available), 3) regional redirect, 4) cost-model swap. each step emits telemetry and is reversible.
iaz: (typo) sorry meant ria
ria: love the graceful-degrade plan. for tenants that explicitly ask for quality in header, skip cost-model swap until the last step. but enforce quota checks.
zach: also ensure circuit-breaker reason is part of trace so ops can correlate cb type (error-rate vs latency vs connection-errors) with fallback step.
alex: ok I'll draft a PR to change chooser to consult: header_hint -> header_whitelist -> quota & capacity checks -> decide or fall through. adding telemetry booleans and policy_source string. will include e2e that simulates CB and asserts header logged and behavior matches policy.
maya: console: add a column in the routes table 'fallback-policy' and in trace viewer add fallback.header_hint and fallback.policy_source. Also add a 'simulate header' quick action for rolls.
ria: final note: if header indicates prefer-primary but tenant not allowed, log a warning with tenant id and header value. Do not change behavior silently.
alex: tagging @maya @zach for review on the PR. i'll include a short oncall playbook: how to interpret fallback.header_hint, how to force a temporary bypass for an emergency customer.
maya: :thumbsup:
ria: thanks — will review the PR when posted.
